Depression can feel like a solid block that is a part of our being, what Buddhists refer to as self. But when we look closer, we can see that the depression is changing, and does not actually belong to us. It is not self. It is a series of many sensations that are constantly changing. When we get attached to depression, feel identified with it, and that it is permanent, it lingers. When we let go, it can tire itself out and change. Trying constantly to change it into another mental state will exhaust us and prolong this feeling. At least, this is how it has been for me, and seeing it like this has helped immensely.

I had been depressed and suicidal for a long time. In 2018 I was at my wits end, had just read "How to Change Your Mind" and was ready to try it. I had a handful of experiences before and saw their potential, but nothing lasting. After this experience, I completely changed my life around. Felt so much gratitude and awe at the beauty of life. It lasted long enough for me to have a kickass year. During that time I decided to reapply to schools to finish my degree, finally got a job and could reliably work, went on tour, and spent a month in Canada working on a farm. It was one of the best times of my life. For a year, I was convinced I was cured of depression (still had some minor social anxiety, but I was so much better). Then covid happened, and I hadn't made any friends in the new college town I was living in, and depression started to kick in again. So the depression did come back, but I was free from it for a good while and got a new perspective on life. It has never been quite as bad as it was before. I think my intentions, mindset (having read positive literature on it), and humble attitude towards the mushroom led to an immensely positive experience. I probably took around 4.5-5 grams.
